name: Question 5
problem:
Express $5\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ in the form $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with $ϕ\in (0,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ Use the **exact value** for $R,$ and round $ϕ$ to **three decimal places**.

$5\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x≈$
{{field-1}}
$\operatorname{sin}⁡(x\,-$
{{field-2}}$)$
worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude–phase form

$$
5\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & =(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=5 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{5} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{2}{5} \\ ϕ & =arctan\,(\frac{2}{5}) \\ ϕ & ≈0.381\,\text{rad},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

For the amplitude,

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{R}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ & ={2}^{2}+{5}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =4+25 \\ {R}^{2} & =29 \\ R & =\sqrt{29}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)≈\sqrt{29}sin\,(x-0.381).
$$
